newsitem.title: USA: Selfix raises '96 EPS view to $0.17-$0.20.
newsitem.headline: Selfix raises '96 EPS view to $0.17-$0.20.

text.p: Selfix Inc said Thursday it had raised its earnings projection for fiscal 1996, ending December 28, to $0.17-$0.20 a share.
Previously, it expected earnings of $0.05-$0.07 a share.
In fiscal 1995 it had a net loss of $1.11 a share, which included a $0.55 restructuring charge.
Selfix, which makes and markets consumer home organization products, said the revised earnings projection follows two consecutive quarters of significantly higher earnings.

"The sweeping changes we've made in the past year have shown a dramatic positive impact in both our second and third quarter," James Tennant, chairman, said in a statement. "We are now confident that the same reengineering initiatives will likewise have a positive impact on our fourth-quarter results."
In the 1995 fourth quarter Selfix reported a loss of $1.03 a share.

Previously, Selfix announced plans to buy Tamor Plastics Corp, a leading supplier of storage and organization products for the home and office. Selfix management previously said they expected the combined company to post sales of about $120 million in 1996.
Based on the anticipated contribution of Tamor operations, Selfix said it expects the transaction to be accretive to net income and earnings per share in 1997 and beyond.
The acquisition is expected to be completed in January.
